jobs.title: Director, Technology Operations & Sustainment
jobs.description:
Description

Leidos Energy | Homeland Sector | Technology

Role Overview

The Director, Technology Operations & Sustainment leads the organization responsible for the effectiveness of Leidos Energy’s current technology baseline, including Business Area-owned networks and specialized energy hardware and software. The team ensures these capabilities are reliable, secure, supported, and effectively used while continuously improving the environment as business needs evolve.

The opportunity is to move beyond traditional technology support and create an environment in which technology measurably improves how Energy employees perform their work. This leader will help shape the technology organization for the combined Leidos Energy business, bringing together the capabilities, experience, and strengths of Leidos and ENTRUST.

Key Responsibilities

Own and Improve the Current Technology Baseline

Lead the operation, sustainment, and lifecycle management of Business Area-owned technology.
Ensure critical capabilities are reliable, secure, resilient, supportable, and appropriate for Energy’s needs.
Simplify the technology environment by addressing obsolescence, unnecessary complexity, fragmentation, and technical debt.
Assume ongoing ownership of new or improved capabilities following successful deployment and transition into the technology baseline.

Enable the Energy Workforce

Develop a strong understanding of how Energy employees use technology to perform engineering, technical, and business work.
Identify and remove technology-related friction, capability gaps, and barriers to effective work.
Improve workflows through better use of existing capabilities, automation, simplification, and user enablement.
Use operational experience and employee feedback to identify opportunities requiring more significant changes to the technology baseline.

Lead Technology Operations

Establish priorities based on business impact, operational risk, user needs, and technology health.
Partner with Innovation & Deployment when significant changes or new capabilities are required.
Manage the organization, portfolio, resources, investments, and external providers necessary to deliver the mission.
Provide the Energy CTO and Business Area leadership with clear insight into technology health, risks, priorities, and investment needs.
Build an effective, engaged team by bringing together existing capabilities, developing people and leaders, and creating opportunities for talent across the combined Energy organization.

Leadership Expectations

Own outcomes, not infrastructure.Measure success by how effectively technology enables the business.
Understand the user.Stay close to employees and how work is actually performed.
Improve while sustaining.Keep critical capabilities operating while continuously making the environment better and simpler.
Lead to yes.Work across security, policy, architecture, and organizational boundaries to find responsible solutions.
Operate as one technology organization.Apply capabilities and resources across team and organizational boundaries to achieve the best business outcome.

Basic Qualifications

Bachelor’s degree in engineering, computer science, information technology, or a related technical discipline and 12+ years of relevant professional experience; equivalent combination of education and experience considered.
Demonstrated experience leading and developing technical organizations and multidisciplinary teams, including developing technical leaders.
Demonstrated leadership of significant operational technology capabilities and experience improving how a technical or engineering workforce uses technology to perform its work.
Ability to translate employee and business needs into technology priorities and communicate technology choices, risks, and tradeoffs clearly to senior business and technical leaders.
Demonstrated ability to simplify complex technology environments and lead across organizational boundaries, including responsibility for significant technology resources, investments, and external providers.

Preferred Qualifications

Master’s degree in a relevant technical or business discipline.
Deep understanding of energy, utility, engineering, or another engineering-intensive business, including how technology enables the work of technical professionals.
Experience modernizing established technology environments while maintaining operational continuity.
Experience operating successfully in a large, matrixed organization.

If you're looking for comfort, keep scrolling. At Leidos, we outthink, outbuild, and outpace the status quo — because the mission demands it. We're not hiring followers. We're recruiting the ones who disrupt, provoke, and refuse to fail. Step 10 is ancient history. We're already at step 30 — and moving faster than anyone else dares.

Original Posting

October 2, 2026

For U.S. Positions: While subject to change based on business needs, Leidos reasonably anticipates that this job requisition will remain open for at least 3 days with an anticipated close date of no earlier than 3 days after the original posting date as listed above.

Pay Range

Pay Range $154,050.00 - $278,475.00

The Leidos pay range for this job level is a general guideline onlyand not a guarantee of compensation or salary. Additional factors considered in extending an offer include (but are not limited to) responsibilities of the job, education, experience, knowledge, skills, and abilities, as well as internal equity, alignment with market data, applicable bargaining agreement (if any), or other law.

About Leidos

Leidos is an industry and technology leader serving government and commercial customers with smarter, more efficient digital and mission innovations. Headquartered in Reston, Virginia, with 47,000 global employees, Leidos reported annual revenues of approximately $16.7 billion for the fiscal year ended January 3, 2025. For more information, visit www.Leidos.com.

Pay And Benefits

Pay and benefits are fundamental to any career decision. That's why we craft compensation packages that reflect the importance of the work we do for our customers. Employment benefits include competitive compensation, Health and Wellness programs, Income Protection, Paid Leave and Retirement. More details are available at www.leidos.com/careers/pay-benefits.

Securing Your Data

Beware of fake employment opportunities using Leidos’ name. Leidos will never ask you to provide payment-related information during any part of the employment application process (i.e., ask you for money), nor will Leidos ever advance money as part of the hiring process (i.e., send you a check or money order before doing any work). Further, Leidos will only communicate with you through emails that are generated by the Leidos.com automated system – never from free commercial services (e.g., Gmail, Yahoo, Hotmail) or via WhatsApp, Telegram, etc. If you received an email purporting to be from Leidos that asks for payment-related information or any other personal information (e.g., about you or your previous employer), and you are concerned about its legitimacy, please make us aware immediately by emailing us at LeidosCareersFraud@leidos.com.

If you believe you are the victim of a scam, contact your local law enforcement and report the incident to the U.S. Federal Trade Commission.

Commitment to Non-Discrimination

All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to sex, race, ethnicity, age, national origin, citizenship, religion, physical or mental disability, medical condition, genetic information, pregnancy, family structure, marital status, ancestry, domestic partner status, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, veteran or military status, or any other basis prohibited by law. Leidos will also consider for employment qualified applicants with criminal histories consistent with relevant laws.

jobs.title: WattBridge- Senior Director, Information Technology
jobs.description:
About WattBridge

The global energy landscape is rapidly changing, and we're here to accelerate that change. From the decommissioning of high-carbon power assets, accelerated expansion of renewable energy resources as baseload power, to the advent of the prosumer. The volatility on today's energy grid has never been greater. WattBridge was conceived by power industry experts to enable the sustained integration of highly efficient, reduced carbon dispatchable power generation assets on our national energy grid.

Position Summary

WattBridge, the world’s preeminent LM6000 delivery platform, is seeking a Senior Director, Information Technology to develop, implement, and own the company’s information technology (IT), cybersecurity and data strategy that will support the origination, development and commercial operations of a full power delivery platform focused on data center campus style development. WattBridge developed, financed, built, owned and operated the world’s largest LM6000 portfolio consisting of 2400 MW’s from 2019 thru 2026. The platform raised over $2BN in capital and is now partnered with Energy Capital Partners as our majority sponsor. With competitive advantages in secured power equipment as an OEM, a proven track record in building out a 2400 MW portfolio, and a fully vertically integrated execution platform, we are well positioned to be highly successful in the data center industry.

The primary focus of this role is developing and leading the separation of IT and cybersecurity services from Parent Company under the Transition Services Agreement (TSA), stands up an independent, cloud-native technology platform within twelve months of close, and then runs that platform through a small internal team and a managed service model. The position builds enterprise-grade IT, cybersecurity, and governance from the outset, secures operational technology (OT) at the company's generation assets, and establishes the controls, reporting, and data foundation expected of a private equity-backed company preparing for future capital markets activity.

Reports to
: Vice President Business Development.

Work Location:
Remote United States

Position Responsibilities

Serve as WattBridge's TSA workstream lead for IT and cybersecurity, coordinating with the PROENERGY counterpart and owning monthly service reviews
Deliver the IT and cybersecurity exit milestones within the 12-month TSA term, including an independent Microsoft 365 tenant, a live MSP contract, and full endpoint migration
Build and execute the 90-day transition plans required before each TSA exit, including knowledge transfer, data migration, and systems access cutover
Enforce WattBridge data ownership and portability rights, ensuring all company data is extracted and validated before TSA systems access ends
Track TSA service levels, cost-plus charges, and scope changes, escalating issues through the governance model defined in the agreement
Define WattBridge's technology strategy and roadmap under the principle of outsourcing infrastructure while owning data and insights
Select cloud-native, low-administration platforms that employee growth and beyond without re-platforming
Partner with Finance, Commercial, Development, and HR leaders to select and deploy core business systems, including ERP, HRIS, project and pipeline management, and document management
Embed AI capabilities from day one, including Microsoft 365 Copilot adoption, a governed AI use-case pipeline, and an enterprise data and analytics foundation (Power BI)
Plan the technology footprint for asset operations if O&M transitions from PROENERGY, including CMMS, asset performance monitoring, and predictive maintenance (AMPS / PI)
Establish and lead the cybersecurity program, including policies, standards, risk management, identity and access management, and incident response
Oversee the managed detection and response (MDR/SOC) partner, Microsoft Defender endpoint protection, vulnerability management, and the incident response retainer
Secure OT/ICS environments at generation assets, including deployment of passive OT monitoring (Claroty or Dragos) and IT/OT segmentation
Ensure compliance with NERC CIP and other applicable regulatory requirements for generation assets, and support audits and regulatory inspections
Run security awareness training and phishing simulation for all employees and contractors
Establish IT governance aligned with NIST CSF, including IT general controls (ITGCs) that support lender reporting, audit, and future SOX readiness
Build and manage the IT and cybersecurity operating and capital budgets, including the one-time Day-1 infrastructure and end-user equipment plan
Report technology risk, cybersecurity posture, and program status to the executive team, PE sponsor, and board as required
Develop business continuity and disaster recovery capability, including backup (Azure Backup), recovery objectives, and tested recovery plans
Lead competitive selection of a Houston-based managed service provider and define contract scope, service level agreements, and performance reporting
Negotiate and manage all technology vendor, licensing, and telecommunications agreements for value and security compliance
Hire, lead, and develop IT staff, setting goals, standards, and on-call expectations
Deliver a consistent onboarding experience as the company scales through each hiring wave, from equipment and accounts on day one to security training

Required Qualifications

Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Information Technology, Information Systems, or a related field
Minimum 15 years of progressive IT experience with 5+ years in IT leadership roles
Proven experience leading an IT carve-out, divestiture separation, or standing up IT for a new or spun-off company
Hands-on experience negotiating, governing, and exiting transition services agreements
Strong background building and leading cybersecurity programs, including OT/ICS security
Deep knowledge of the Microsoft cloud ecosystem (Microsoft 365, Entra ID, Intune, Defender, Azure)
Experience selecting and managing MSP and MDR/SOC providers against defined service levels
Working knowledge of NERC CIP compliance and critical infrastructure regulatory requirements
Experience deploying or supporting core business systems such as ERP, HRIS, and document management platforms
Proven ability to build a lean technology function that relies on outsourced services while retaining ownership of data and architecture
Strong budget management, vendor negotiation, and contract management skills
Excellent executive communication skills, with the ability to explain technology risk and investment in business terms
Ability to operate hands-on in a small, fast-moving organization while setting enterprise-grade standards
Must be fluent in English, with strong speaking, reading, writing, and comprehension skills.
Successful candidate will need to satisfactorily complete pre-employment drug screen and background check
US work authorization is a precondition of employment. The company will not consider candidates who require sponsorship for a work-authorized visa.

Desired Qualifications

Experience in power generation, independent power producers, utilities, or other critical infrastructure
Experience in a private equity-backed company, including sponsor reporting and exit or IPO readiness
Knowledge of SOX IT general controls and audit support
Experience deploying Microsoft 365 Copilot and building an AI governance and use-case program
Familiarity with OT asset visibility and monitoring platforms such as Claroty, Dragos, or Nozomi
Knowledge of OSIsoft PI / AVEVA PI, historian, and asset performance management platforms
Familiarity with ERCOT market operations and generation asset connectivity
Experience with Power BI and building enterprise data and reporting foundations

Certifications

CISSP, CISM, or equivalent security leadership certification
GIAC Global Industrial Cyber Security Professional (GICSP) or equivalent OT security credential
ITIL 4 Foundation for service management
Project Management (PMP) or equivalent credentials

It is PROENERGY’s policy to provide equal opportunity in employment to all its employees and applicants for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, pregnancy, age, disability, national origin, marital status, ancestry, medical condition, military status, or any other characteristic protected by State or Federal law.
